findings: src/input/controls.ts:37-42,117-120 + src/main.tsx:25-29 — expected: the floating joystick ring appears under the thumb and the HUD stays put — observed: Controls appends the .joy-base div into .layer BEFORE render(<App/>, layer); Preact reuses that div as the root <div class="ui">, so showJoy() writes translate(x-56px, y-56px) onto the whole UI. After the first joystick drag the money card jumps to mid-screen, the nav bar and HUSTLE button go off-screen, and no joystick is drawn. The test's own artifact e2e/__shots__/controls-lotcard.png shows this, yet F14 passes and F13 says the screenshots were 'reviewed by eye' — how to reproduce: npm run build:test && npx playwright test e2e/controls.spec.ts, then open e2e/__shots__/controls-lotcard.png; or run node .eval/ctrl.mjs (preview on :4180): document.querySelector('.ui').getBoundingClientRect().top goes 0 -> 504 after one drag at (90,560).

src/core/mechanics.ts:47-64, src/core/trade.ts:39, tests/helpers/bot.ts — expected (owner's top priority): the starting region changes what you actually do in the first 10-20 minutes — observed: with the real sim and the balance bot, the best play is the same everywhere: spam Street Food Carts and Kiosks. At 20 min the empires are Ironhold 19 carts + 6 kiosks and zero industry, Solenne 14 carts + 7 kiosks and zero logistics, Neon Vale (seed 7) 15 carts + 5 kiosks and zero tech. The signature mechanics only touch agri, energy, tech, hospitality and industry, which are not worth buying early. Solenne's Free Port does nothing for a player based in Solenne: imports into Solenne are tariff-free, but transshipping from Solenne is blocked. So for the first minutes the regions differ only in prices, hustle amounts and event flavour text — how to reproduce: npx vitest run --config .eval/vitest.config.ts .eval/early.test.ts (prints owned businesses per region at 20 min).

src/core/data/regions.ts:111-112,154,195-196,238 (shown on the region-select cards via src/ui/RegionSelect.tsx:58-62) and docs/GDD.md §5 — expected: the numbers on the region cards match the game — observed: the cards promise 'Tech income x2', 'hype x0.6-x1.7', 'harvest x2.0 / winter x0.4', 'high season x1.8 / Tourism x1.9' and 'Industry x1.8'. In code, BAL.demandSpread 0.35 (src/core/balance.ts:6) squeezes demand to x1.35 for tech, x1.28 for industry and x1.32 for hospitality, and mechanics.ts:12,23-27 uses seasons 0.75/1.0/1.6/0.5, tourism 1.5/0.7 and hype 0.7-1.5. The region pitch overstates every signature by 30-100 % — how to reproduce: compare the select screen (e2e/__shots__/select.png) with demandMult()/SEASON_MULT/TOURISM_*/HYPE_* in a vitest REPL.

src/ui/LotCard.tsx:180-184 (fitLabel) — expected: the '≈ $/s' shown before you buy roughly matches what the business earns — observed: the estimate leaves out income tax, upkeep, competition and law modifiers. Neon Vale kiosk: card ≈$11.04/s, actual $2.92/s (+278 %). Ironhold cart: +158 %. Solenne kiosk: +145 %. Every region is overstated by 23-278 %. In the browser, a Solenne cart is listed at '≈ $1.1/s' and earns $0.4/s once bought, which teaches players to distrust the card — how to reproduce: npx vitest run --config .eval/vitest.config.ts .eval/est.test.ts; or in the game, tap a vacant small lot, note ≈$/s, build a cart, and read INCOME.

src/world/World.ts:188-197 (rebuildCity) — expected: smooth 60 fps on phones ('optimised') — observed: the whole city's merged geometry plus smoke is rebuilt whenever any lot in the current region changes business or crosses a 10-level band. Each rebuild took 46-74 ms on the sandbox CPU (rebuildMs in .eval/play.log), and the real sim triggers 112-144 rebuilds per 10 minutes (one every ~4.5 s), mostly from rival purchases and NPC churn the player didn't cause. That is a 3-4-frame hitch every few seconds on a desktop CPU, and worse on a mid-range phone — how to reproduce: npx vitest run --config .eval/vitest.config.ts .eval/rebuild.test.ts (rebuild count), and in preview: performance.now() around __BR.session.world.rebuildCity(__BR.state().regions[__BR.state().currentRegion].lots).

src/world/buildings.ts:299-316, src/world/scenery.ts:94-107, docs/ART_BIBLE.md — expected: a distinct 'sunlit diorama' with no generic boxes, and a first screen that sells each region — observed: (a) the player spawns facing the same City Hall model in all six regions, with only the dome and stone tint changed, so the six first screens are near-identical (e2e/__shots__/world-*-day.png). (b) Palm fronds are 8 flat planks, which read as propellers (world-verano-day.png, world-solenne-day.png). (c) The follow camera is so close that one roof or factory fills the bottom ~40 % of the screen (world-solenne-day.png, world-amberfield-day.png, world-amberfield-wide.png). (d) Nights are muddy, near-black masses (world-redmesa-night.png, world-amberfield-night.png). (e) Neon Vale night windows render as grey/white checkerboards with little neon (world-neonvale-night.png). (f) Verano's sand reads as grey-white, not #f4e7c5. As it stands this would look 'mid' on the App Store — how to reproduce: npm run build:test && npx playwright test e2e/world.spec.ts, then view e2e/__shots__/world-*.png.

src/core/rivals.ts:191 + src/app/session.ts:191-197 + src/ui/styles.css:262,266 — expected: notifications that never cover the play area or modals — observed: NPC-churn notices ('For sale: the old X just closed') are kind 'info' and not throttled; only 'rival' is. Up to three large toasts stack at top:212px over the middle third of the screen in every region (world-*-night.png, .eval/shots/*-8-later.png). Toasts also draw over the event modal's header (.eval/shots/redmesa-7-event.png), and the RANK UP banner overlaps the lot card and the Politics law grid (e2e/__shots__/ui-vacant.png, ui-sheet-politics.png). Each purchase also produces two toasts (ui-event.png) — how to reproduce: start any region and __BR.advance(190); or rank up while a lot card is open.

src/core/actions.ts:267-275 + src/core/mechanics.ts:104 — expected: Ironhold's Union Mood forces a real trade-off — observed: 'Sign wage deal' costs no cash and gives +25 mood. Three taps set wageDeal to 0.3, which multiplies mood erosion by max(0.1, 1-0.96) = 0.1, in exchange for about +3.6 % upkeep. Strikes then effectively never happen, and the region's signature mechanic is switched off by three free taps — how to reproduce: newGame('ironhold'), signWageDeal x3, place 10 machine shops, advance 30 min: unionMood stays above 30 and no strike occurs.

src/core/mechanics.ts:38, src/core/events.ts:59,116, src/core/politics.ts:89 — expected: faction standing, which events and donations advertise ('+15 standing'), changes something — observed: standing is read in only one place, where Red Mesa Circle standing ≥50 halves permit waits. For the other 17 factions it is display-only. rm_nephew 'Refuse — your next permit may take a while' (events.ts:140) does nothing because negative standing never lengthens permits — how to reproduce: grep -n 'standing' src --include=*.ts; resolve rm_nephew with 'Refuse' and compare permitWait() before and after.

src/core/rivals.ts:112 — expected: following the toast's advice ends the price war — observed: the toast says 'Buy them out of the district to stop it', but the war buff is removed only by acquireRival (rivals.ts:251). buyRivalLot (rivals.ts:206-223) leaves the -35 % in place for the full 2 minutes — how to reproduce: trigger a price war, buy the rival's same-category lot in that district, and check that state.buffs still contains 'war:<rival>' and that your income is still x0.65.

src/core/data/regions.ts difficulty fields + tests/balance.test.ts:38-42 — expected: the difficulty stars predict how hard a region is — observed: 45-minute bot net worth in purchasing-power terms (net worth / cost index, seed 21): Red Mesa (3 stars, 'Hard') $17.6M; Solenne (2 stars) $3.25M; Ironhold (3 stars) $3.5M; Verano (2 stars) $11.4M; Amberfield (1 star) $23M; Neon Vale (4 stars) $1.9M. Hard Red Mesa is 5x easier than Standard Solenne, and the test only checks Amberfield > Neon Vale — how to reproduce: npm run ci and read the [balance] lines.

docs/ART_BIBLE.md juice rules vs src/world/World.ts:193 — expected: buildings 'grow' with squash-and-stretch when upgraded, and every upgrade feels visible — observed: there is no squash/stretch or upgrade tween anywhere in src/world (the only scale animation is the selection ring pulse in markers.ts:139). Geometry changes only every 10 levels, so levels 1-9 of every business look the same — how to reproduce: grep -rn 'squash\|stretch' src; upgrade a cart from L1 to L9 and watch the world.

e2e/controls.spec.ts:39-41, e2e/ui.spec.ts:20-24, features.json F15/F16/F1 — expected: e2e tests that would fail on the bugs above, and evidence that matches the claims — observed: the controls test asserts only that the lot card is visible in the DOM, so it passes while the HUD is displaced off-screen. ui.spec's 'buy flow from the world' uses b.give(5000), b.teleport and session.select instead of tapping or walking. F16's 'published playtest link works' rests on a 302 to a sign-in page, so it is ASSUMED, not VERIFIED. F1 is still passes:false although npm run ci is green — how to reproduce: read the specs; add an assertion that .hud and [data-testid=hustle] stay inside the viewport after the joystick swipe, and it fails today.

src/core/rivals.ts:116-128 + src/core/events.ts:34-47 — expected: a varied early event stream — observed: in a fresh browser run, the first event in 5 of 6 regions within ~4 minutes was 'An Offer You Could Refuse' for a single $60-$130 cart ('Sable Ridge Minerals wants to buy your Street Food Cart for $84'). rival_offer and sabotage appear in every region's 20-minute event list in the bot runs, crowding out region-only events early — how to reproduce: node .eval/play.mjs and read events[] per region in .eval/play.log; or .eval/early.test.ts.
